_sources.discrepancies: Wisconsin has a strict photo ID requirement per NCSL. The Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC) confirms a wide range of acceptable photo IDs including Wisconsin ID cards, driver licenses, military IDs, tribal IDs, and student IDs from Wisconsin accredited schools. Voters without ID may receive a free Wisconsin voter ID from the DMV. Wisconsin primary is the second Tuesday in August per statute. Same-day registration is available in Wisconsin through Election Day. 2026-06-10 verification: August 11, 2026 primary CONFIRMED (FVAP calendar current as of May 2026). Online registration deadline corrected — online (like mail) registration closes 20 days before the election per myvote.wi.gov (July 22 / October 14); the file previously showed online open through Election Day. In-person absentee window corrected to the statutory rule: begins no earlier than 14 days before the election and ends no later than the Sunday before (primary July 28-Aug 9; general Oct 20-Nov 1); exact days/hours are set by each municipal clerk.

earlyVoting.notes: In-person absentee voting at municipal clerk offices may begin no earlier than 14 days before the primary (July 28, 2026) and ends no later than the Sunday before (August 9, 2026). Days and hours are set by each municipal clerk — check myvote.wi.gov.

In-person absentee voting at municipal clerk offices may begin no earlier than 14 days before Election Day (October 20, 2026) and ends no later than the Sunday before (November 1, 2026). Days and hours are set by each municipal clerk — check myvote.wi.gov.

In-person absentee voting at municipal clerk offices runs from no earlier than 14 days before Election Day through the Sunday before; days and hours are set by each municipal clerk. Same-day registration is available at the polls on Election Day with proof of residence.

acceptedIds: Wisconsin driver's license or state ID card (unexpired, or expired after the most recent general election)
U.S. military ID with expiration date or issuance date within 2 years
Student ID from a Wisconsin accredited institution (with signature and expiration date)
Employee ID from a Wisconsin government employer
Wisconsin voter ID card (free from the DMV)
votingRules.expirationRule: A Wisconsin driver's license or state ID may be used if it expired after the most recent general election. Student IDs must be unexpired or expired no more than 2 years. Details: https://elections.wi.gov/voters/photo-id-law
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without acceptable ID may obtain a free Wisconsin voter ID card from any DMV service center before Election Day.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Wisconsin allows phones at polling places but prohibits photography that reveals how a voter marked their ballot. No electioneering within 100 feet of the polling place entrance.
additionalRules: Open primary: voters do not register by party; voters choose which party's primary ballot to vote on election day.
Same-day voter registration available on Election Day with proof of residence.
No runoffs in Wisconsin — the candidate with the most votes wins.
Free photo ID is available from any Wisconsin DMV service center.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: 5 p.m. on the Thursday before the election for online/mail requests; in-person absentee available through the Sunday before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the municipal clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the municipal clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Wisconsin has an open primary (Wis. Stat. §5.60). Any registered voter may vote in either party's primary. Voters may not split their vote between parties — they must vote on a single party's ballot.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Wisconsin tiene una primaria abierta (Wis. Stat. §5.60). Cualquier votante registrado puede votar en la primaria de cualquier partido. Los votantes no pueden dividir su voto entre partidos: deben votar en la boleta de un solo partido.
